Now that dotnet 11 is out, 
lets reimagine this whole project for dotnet 11 
if you were writing this project from scratch today 
what would you do differently? 
do that 
for example, 
we do need to worry about backward compatibility when it comes to our output 
the existing file structure must be preserved 
no existing emails should be deleted ever 
do not break user's data
other than that we have free reign to change things 
even force a clean out of the search caches and rebuild if required 
but only if required, not just for fun 
it must have a valid justificatiion if we do it
and make our code cleaner and leaner 
there may be new things we could do in dotnet 11 and csharp 15
do them the new way when and where possible 
there might also be code that we won't need with dotnet 11
also there might be nuget packages and github actions 
and other dependencies that we can upgrade to latest stable as well
upgrade them all 
as we do all of this 
please be mindful to use best engineering practices 
and solid principles 
Use your best judgment
If only a few files (under five or there about) need to change, give me the full path of the files that need to change and the FULL file 
if there are a lot of files that need to change 
Delivery
    Whole project as one tar.gz, unambiguous file placement
    do not include any file that has not changed 
    Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly
    No bespoke sed/patch scripts — full files only for anything that changes
    Docs updated alongside code changes
    Low verbosity, no code comments
    I only have the rc3 locally so the CI will need to do everything
    unless you can structure the global.json to work with rc3 or better
    this will improve soon when dotnet 11 stable lands on fedora default repos 
one another fly in the ointment 
my laptop only has rc3 
so this new code will need to work with rc3 locally 
but use the latest stable build on github actions

lets reimagine this whole project for dotnet 11 
if you were writing this project from scratch today 
what would you do differently? 
do that 
for example, 
we do need to worry about backward compatibility when it comes to our output 
the existing file structure must be preserved 
no existing emails should be deleted ever 
do not break user's data
other than that we have free reign to change things 
even force a clean out of the search caches and rebuild if required 
but only if required, not just for fun 
it must have a valid justificatiion if we do it
and make our code cleaner and leaner 
there may be new things we could do in dotnet 11 and csharp 15
do them the new way when and where possible 
there might also be code that we won't need with dotnet 11

and other dependencies that we can upgrade to latest stable as well

Ran 72 commands, read 27 pages, and 31 more tools
Slice 75 is packaged as myrestaurant-slice-75-dotnet-11.tar.gz (28 changed or new files, extract at the repo root), but nothing in it has been compiled. This sandbox has no .NET SDK and can’t reach NuGet, so your rc3 build is the first real check. The tree-hygiene and governance scripts pass here, and the Markdown-table and version gates pass in emulation.

Your message talks about emails and search caches and the dotnet --info is from MyImapDownloader, but the project, dump.txt and terminal.txt are all myrestaurant. I applied the same rules there: no schema, migration, route, cookie or stored format changed, and nothing is cleared or rebuilt on upgrade.

Why the tests don’t complete
terminal.txt shows the PostgreSQL containers created and running while both container-backed assemblies sat at zero tests for 42 minutes. run.sh --smoke reached a containerised PostgreSQL on the same host in the same session. The difference is how the fixtures decide readiness: pg_isready through the engine’s exec endpoint, with no deadline and the logger silenced. That started after Fedora 44 → 45, which moved Podman 5 → 6.

I could not observe which call stalled, so the fix doesn’t depend on it:

Readiness from the host: a SELECT 1 over the published port instead of exec.
Five-minute deadline: a timeout now fails with the container’s state and log tail. No engine at all is still a skip.
One server for the data-access assembly: each test class gets its own database instead of its own container. No test class changed.
Your podman ps -a also shows dozens of orphaned postgres containers from the hung runs, which are worth pruning.

.NET 11
SDK: global.json names rc3 as a floor with rollForward: latestMinor, so your laptop builds on rc3 and CI installs stable 11.0.x. When Fedora ships stable, you move with no edit.
Target and images: net11.0, sdk:11.0 and aspnet:11.0.
Removed: the OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore package, because ASP.NET Core 11 emits that telemetry natively.
C# 15: OrderOperation is now a closed hierarchy, so a switch that misses an operation kind is a build error; four runtime fallback arms are gone.
Lock: RestaurantTime locks on System.Threading.Lock.
Left alone
NuGet and Actions: your own dotnet list package --outdated from today reports no updates, and the Actions I could check are on their latest major (actions/cache I couldn’t check).
PostgreSQL 17: a new major means a dump-and-restore of your data, so it belongs in its own slice.
To apply
bash
git rm tests/MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tests/ContainerEngineDiscovery.cs
git rm tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/ContainerEngineDiscovery.cs
tar -xzf myrestaurant-slice-75-dotnet-11.tar.gz
git add -A
Both deletes are required: the class now lives in tests/Shared/, and leaving either old copy is a duplicate-type build error.

Most likely to fail on first build
closed: taken from the C# 15 reference, never through a compiler here.
The custom wait strategy: I read the Testcontainers 4.16.0 source for everything except AddCustomWaitStrategy, whose page wouldn’t load.
New .NET 11 analyzer warnings: CI treats warnings as errors, so any new rule that fires on existing code turns CI red even if your local build passes.
Expected test count is unchanged at 1332. _CHANGES.md has a reversal for each of the riskier changes.

Now the platform edits.Now the documentation edits.Now the ledger, build log, operations note and `_CHANGES.md`.Four columns: wrong / ruling / where. Splitting my rows at "**Ruled:**".Slice 75 is packaged as `myrestaurant-slice-75-dotnet-11.tar.gz` (28 changed or new files, extract at the repo root), but nothing in it has been compiled. This sandbox has no .NET SDK and can't reach NuGet, so your rc3 build is the first real check. The tree-hygiene and governance scripts pass here, and the Markdown-table and version gates pass in emulation.

Your message talks about emails and search caches and the `dotnet --info` is from MyImapDownloader, but the project, `dump.txt` and `terminal.txt` are all myrestaurant. I applied the same rules there: no schema, migration, route, cookie or stored format changed, and nothing is cleared or rebuilt on upgrade.

## Why the tests don't complete

`terminal.txt` shows the PostgreSQL containers created and running while both container-backed assemblies sat at zero tests for 42 minutes. `run.sh --smoke` reached a containerised PostgreSQL on the same host in the same session. The difference is how the fixtures decide readiness: `pg_isready` through the engine's exec endpoint, with no deadline and the logger silenced. That started after Fedora 44 → 45, which moved Podman 5 → 6.

I could not observe which call stalled, so the fix doesn't depend on it:

- **Readiness from the host:** a `SELECT 1` over the published port instead of exec.
- **Five-minute deadline:** a timeout now fails with the container's state and log tail. No engine at all is still a skip.
- **One server for the data-access assembly:** each test class gets its own database instead of its own container. No test class changed.

Your `podman ps -a` also shows dozens of orphaned postgres containers from the hung runs, which are worth pruning.

## .NET 11

- **SDK:** `global.json` names rc3 as a floor with `rollForward: latestMinor`, so your laptop builds on rc3 and CI installs stable `11.0.x`. When Fedora ships stable, you move with no edit.
- **Target and images:** `net11.0`, `sdk:11.0` and `aspnet:11.0`.
- **Removed:** the `OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore` package, because ASP.NET Core 11 emits that telemetry natively.
- **C# 15:** `OrderOperation` is now a `closed` hierarchy, so a switch that misses an operation kind is a build error; four runtime fallback arms are gone.
- **Lock:** `RestaurantTime` locks on `System.Threading.Lock`.

## Left alone

- **NuGet and Actions:** your own `dotnet list package --outdated` from today reports no updates, and the Actions I could check are on their latest major (`actions/cache` I couldn't check).
- **PostgreSQL 17:** a new major means a dump-and-restore of your data, so it belongs in its own slice.

## To apply

```bash
git rm tests/MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tests/ContainerEngineDiscovery.cs
git rm tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/ContainerEngineDiscovery.cs
tar -xzf myrestaurant-slice-75-dotnet-11.tar.gz
git add -A
```

Both deletes are required: the class now lives in `tests/Shared/`, and leaving either old copy is a duplicate-type build error.

## Most likely to fail on first build

- **`closed`:** taken from the C# 15 reference, never through a compiler here.
- **The custom wait strategy:** I read the Testcontainers 4.16.0 source for everything except `AddCustomWaitStrategy`, whose page wouldn't load.
- **New .NET 11 analyzer warnings:** CI treats warnings as errors, so any new rule that fires on existing code turns CI red even if your local build passes.

Expected test count is unchanged at 1332. `_CHANGES.md` has a reversal for each of the riskier changes.

Sources:

- [What's new in ASP.NET Core 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-11?view=aspnetcore-10.0)
- [Breaking changes in ASP.NET Core 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/breaking-changes/11/overview?view=aspnetcore-10.0)
